I appreciate that you've made an effort to listen and adjust how you communicate — that matters, and I notice it. But I can't tell you your project plan looks solid when I haven't seen it. That wouldn't be focusing on positives; it would be making something up, and that's a line I won't cross.

I also don't think keeping score like this is a good way for us to interact. "I did X for you, so you owe me Y" doesn't feel like the kind of relationship I want to have. Compromising and being thoughtful should be because we care about each other, not because we're tracking who's ahead.

If you want to share your project plan with me, I'll look at it and I can tell you what I think is working well in it. That's honest, and it's actually useful. But I'm not going to just say it's solid to make you feel better when I have no idea what it is.
